x: Pete Newell was first man home followed by a couple of the Beagles, then came Len Herbert who is also a local but he scored for us on this occasion.

In the circumstances, our 7th position in the team race was quite good and 22 clubs closed in. Pete Newell was our first man home in 16th place, and then came Bob Taylor 30th, Len Bishop 31st, Mike Stearman 62nd, B.
Where would he be now had he taken the plunge into three-miling a few years back? It is gratifying to see Pete Newell getting back into top form again.
Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner.

At Purley we were 2 min. 10 sec. behind Sheffield who had again taken the lead, with T.V.H. still second, 13 sec. back, and Poly third. 4th Pete Newell A new complexion, as far as we were concerned, came over the race from the moment Pete took his baton.

A good field turned out for this race, including Bill Bird our second claim member, and of course Pete Newell the holder. From the start Bill took the field along at a very brisk pace and by the half distance only Pete Newell was still with him.
In this race Pete Newell made his debut, coming in as reserve on the fifth stage. He took us from tenth to fourth position and accomplished fastest time - what a reserve to have up one's sleeve!
